title: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Full pathway by disease state (newly diagnosed, on-treatment restaging, relapsed/refractory, surveillance), then pathology/cell-of-origin and MYC/BCL2/BCL6 status -> Ann Arbor stage -> limited vs advanced first-line, each induction refined by CNS risk / fitness / biology / IPI -> a response-adapted restaging step -> complete response to surveillance, residual disease into the relapsed/refractory line-of-therapy sub-tree (CAR-T vs salvage + autologous transplant, then post-cellular options; non-transplant line by prior therapy through bispecifics). Every systemic-therapy leaf references an APPLICABLE dose protocol: the existing R-CHOP Standard Protocol where it fits, plus DRAFT cancer-prefixed protocols authored for this disease (pola-R-CHP, DA-EPOCH-R, R-mini-CHOP, anthracycline-sparing R-GCVP, HD-methotrexate and intrathecal CNS prophylaxis, fludarabine/cyclophosphamide CAR-T lymphodepletion, R-ICE / R-DHAP / R-GDP salvage, BEAM autologous-transplant conditioning, pola-BR, tafasitamab-lenalidomide, R-GemOx, glofitamab, epcoritamab, loncastuximab tesirine). The CAR-T cell product, autologous transplant, allogeneic transplant, and clinical-trial steps are shown as checklist guidance; where a computable chemotherapy accompanies them (lymphodepletion, conditioning) that dose protocol is linked. Surveillance carries no protocol. Workup / staging / risk-stratification content is standard oncology, not proprietary guideline text; structure consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) B-Cell Lymphomas, no proprietary content reproduced. Invents no dose/regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN), B-Cell Lymphomas. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols where one clinically fits; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Risk in DLBCL is scored by the International Prognostic Index (IPI): one point each for age >60, stage III-IV, elevated LDH, ECOG >=2, and >1 extranodal site. The NCCN-IPI refines age and LDH into graded bands. Higher score predicts a lower cure rate and helps select treatment intensity.

b.text: For previously untreated patients with intermediate-to-high risk (IPI 2-5), substituting polatuzumab vedotin for vincristine (pola-R-CHP) improved progression-free survival versus R-CHOP in a randomized trial, with similar overall survival at first report.

c.text: CNS prophylaxis is considered for patients at high risk of central-nervous-system relapse (high CNS-IPI, or high-risk sites such as testis, breast, kidney/adrenal, paranasal sinus, or epidural). Options include high-dose intravenous methotrexate and/or intrathecal chemotherapy. Benefit is debated; the physician weighs risk against toxicity.

d.text: In primary-refractory disease or relapse within 12 months of first-line chemoimmunotherapy, second-line CD19 CAR T-cell therapy (axicabtagene ciloleucel or lisocabtagene maraleucel) improved event-free survival versus salvage chemotherapy plus autologous transplant in randomized trials. Late relapse (>=12 months) remains a candidate for salvage + autologous transplant.

e.text: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 (and/or BCL6) rearrangement (double- / triple-hit) carries a poorer prognosis with R-CHOP. Intensified dose-adjusted EPOCH-R is commonly used in fit patients, with CNS-directed prophylaxis given the elevated CNS-relapse risk; a randomized survival advantage is not established.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and diagnosis
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation once DLBCL is suspected or confirmed. Establish histology, extent of disease, and fitness before therapy.
bullets: Excisional or core biopsy with expert hematopathology review; confirm CD20-positive large B-cell histology (avoid relying on fine-needle aspirate alone)
Immunohistochemistry and cell-of-origin (CD20, CD10, BCL6, MUM1; Hans algorithm: germinal-center vs non-germinal-center)
FISH for MYC, and if positive for BCL2 and BCL6, to identify high-grade double- or triple-hit lymphoma
Contrast CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis and whole-body FDG-PET/CT for staging; bone-marrow biopsy if PET is equivocal for marrow
CBC, complete metabolic panel, LDH, uric acid; hepatitis B/C and HIV serology; baseline echo/MUGA before anthracycline; assess CNS risk and fertility

nodes.name: Disease state
nodes.title: Disease state
nodes.description: Choose the current clinical state. This drives whether to enter the newly-diagnosed staging pathway, the response-assessment step, the relapsed / refractory pathway, or surveillance.

options.label: On / end of first-line therapy - response assessment
Relapsed or refractory after prior therapy

nodes.name: Pathology / biomarker
nodes.title: Pathology and biomarker subtype
nodes.description: Confirm the biology. Cell-of-origin and MYC / BCL2 / BCL6 rearrangement status separate ordinary DLBCL from high-grade double- / triple-hit lymphoma and from transformed indolent lymphoma, which are treated differently.

tables.title: Cell-of-origin and rearrangement subtypes
rows: CD20+ large B-cells; Hans GCB vs non-GCB by IHC
Standard R-CHOP backbone; pola-R-CHP if IPI 2-5
MYC rearrangement plus BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement
Consider intensified DA-EPOCH-R; higher CNS risk
Large-cell transformation of prior low-grade lymphoma
Treat as DLBCL; prior therapy affects options

nodes.name: Transformed: prior therapy
nodes.title: Transformed indolent lymphoma: prior therapy
nodes.description: Large-cell transformation of a previously indolent lymphoma is treated as DLBCL, but prior chemoimmunotherapy for the low-grade disease changes the options and the intent.

nodes.name: Ann Arbor stage
nodes.title: Staging and disease extent
nodes.description: Assign Ann Arbor stage from PET/CT. Limited (non-bulky I-II) and advanced (III-IV, or bulky II) disease follow different first-line pathways.

tables.title: Ann Arbor stage (Lugano modification)
rows: One node region or one extranodal site
Two or more node regions on the same side of the diaphragm
Node regions on both sides of the diaphragm
Diffuse extranodal involvement (e.g. marrow, liver, lung)
Bulky mass (commonly >=7.5 cm) or B symptoms modify risk

nodes.name: Limited risk
nodes.title: Limited-stage: risk features
nodes.description: Within limited stage, the presence of bulk or adverse risk factors (elevated LDH, age >60, ECOG >=2, stage II) determines whether an abbreviated PET-guided course or a full course is used.

nodes.name: Interim PET
nodes.title: Favorable limited: PET-guided abbreviation
nodes.description: For favorable non-bulky disease an interim FDG-PET after a few cycles guides whether a shortened course (chemoimmunotherapy plus involved-site radiation, or a slightly longer chemo-only course) is sufficient.

nodes.name: Abbreviated R-CHOP
nodes.title: Favorable limited, PET-negative: abbreviated R-CHOP
nodes.description: PET-negative favorable limited-stage disease can be cured with a shortened course; then response is confirmed.
bullets: R-CHOP x 3 cycles followed by involved-site radiation, OR R-CHOP x 4-6 cycles with no radiation
Confirm end-of-treatment PET (Deauville 1-3) documents complete metabolic response
Growth-factor support and tumor-lysis prophylaxis as indicated
The dose engine computes the R-CHOP regimen referenced below; then go to response assessment

nodes.name: Extended R-CHOP + RT
nodes.title: Favorable limited, PET-positive: extend R-CHOP + radiation
nodes.description: A positive interim PET calls for a full course and, usually, consolidative radiation to residual disease; then response is confirmed.
bullets: Complete R-CHOP to 6 cycles and add involved-site radiation to the PET-positive site
Biopsy a persistently PET-positive residual mass to exclude refractory disease
Reassess CNS-relapse risk if adverse features emerge
R-CHOP regimen referenced below; then go to response assessment

nodes.name: Full R-CHOP +/- RT
nodes.title: Unfavorable limited: full R-CHOP +/- radiation
nodes.description: Bulky or adverse-factor limited disease is treated like advanced disease with a full course, with radiation to bulk; then response is confirmed.
bullets: R-CHOP x 6 cycles
Consolidative radiation to sites of bulky disease
Consider CNS-risk assessment as for advanced disease
R-CHOP regimen referenced below; then go to response assessment

nodes.name: CNS risk
nodes.title: Advanced: CNS-relapse risk
nodes.description: Before or alongside systemic therapy, stratify CNS-relapse risk (CNS-IPI plus high-risk anatomic sites) to decide on prophylaxis.

tables.title: CNS-IPI risk factors
rows: Age >60, elevated LDH, ECOG >=2, stage III-IV, >1 extranodal site
Testis, breast, epidural, paranasal sinus, uterus - consider prophylaxis regardless of score

nodes.name: CNS prophylaxis
nodes.title: High CNS risk: add prophylaxis, then systemic therapy
nodes.description: Add CNS-directed prophylaxis, then continue to fitness-directed systemic chemoimmunotherapy.
bullets: High-dose intravenous methotrexate and/or intrathecal chemotherapy alongside the systemic regimen
Lumbar puncture with cytology and flow cytometry if not already done; treat overt CNS disease directly
Benefit of prophylaxis is uncertain - individualize against renal function and toxicity
Then proceed to fitness-directed systemic therapy (next step)
CNS-prophylaxis dose protocols referenced below (high-dose IV methotrexate and intrathecal chemotherapy)

nodes.name: Fitness
nodes.title: Advanced: fitness for full-dose therapy
nodes.description: Physiologic fitness and cardiac reserve determine whether full-dose anthracycline-based therapy or an attenuated regimen is appropriate.

nodes.name: Frail regimen
nodes.title: Frail / elderly: regimen selection
nodes.description: For patients unfit for full-dose therapy, ejection fraction and reserve decide between attenuated anthracycline and an anthracycline-sparing backbone; both preserve curative intent where possible.

nodes.name: R-mini-CHOP
nodes.title: Frail, adequate EF: attenuated R-mini-CHOP
nodes.description: A reduced-intensity anthracycline regimen preserves curative intent while limiting toxicity; then response is confirmed.
bullets: R-mini-CHOP (attenuated doses) for patients over about 80 or with limited reserve
Pre-phase steroids, growth-factor support, and infection prophylaxis
Careful cardiac monitoring during anthracycline exposure
Attenuated R-mini-CHOP dose protocol referenced below (accurate reduced doses); then go to response assessment

nodes.name: Anthracycline-sparing
nodes.title: Frail, low EF: anthracycline-sparing regimen
nodes.description: When anthracycline is contraindicated, an anthracycline-sparing or liposomal-anthracycline backbone is used; then response is confirmed.
bullets: R-CEOP (etoposide substituting for doxorubicin) or liposomal-doxorubicin-based backbone for low EF
Pre-phase steroids, growth-factor support, and infection prophylaxis
Serial cardiac assessment; involve cardio-oncology where available
Anthracycline-sparing R-GCVP dose protocol referenced below; then go to response assessment

nodes.name: Advanced biology
nodes.title: Advanced (fit): double-hit vs standard biology
nodes.description: High-grade double- / triple-hit lymphoma may warrant an intensified regimen; otherwise proceed to IPI-directed backbone selection.

nodes.name: Double-hit regimen
nodes.title: Double-hit: intensity of induction
nodes.description: Fit patients with double- / triple-hit lymphoma are often escalated to a dose-adjusted infusional regimen; less-fit patients may still receive R-CHOP with CNS prophylaxis.

nodes.name: DA-EPOCH-R
nodes.title: Double-hit, fit: intensified DA-EPOCH-R
nodes.description: High-grade double- / triple-hit lymphoma is often treated with a dose-adjusted infusional regimen with CNS prophylaxis; then response is confirmed.
bullets: Dose-adjusted EPOCH-R (rituximab, etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) escalated by nadir counts
Include CNS prophylaxis given the higher CNS-relapse risk
Growth-factor support mandatory; monitor for neuropathy and cytopenias
Enroll in a trial where available; DA-EPOCH-R dose protocol referenced below; then go to response assessment

nodes.name: R-CHOP + CNS prophylaxis
nodes.title: Double-hit, less fit: R-CHOP + CNS prophylaxis
nodes.description: For double-hit patients unfit for intensified therapy, R-CHOP with CNS prophylaxis remains an option; then response is confirmed.
bullets: R-CHOP x 6 cycles with high-dose methotrexate and/or intrathecal CNS prophylaxis
Reassess fitness for escalation if tolerance is good
Growth-factor support and tumor-lysis prophylaxis
R-CHOP regimen referenced below; then go to response assessment

nodes.name: IPI selection
nodes.title: Advanced (fit, standard): IPI-directed backbone
nodes.description: IPI risk selects between the R-CHOP backbone and the polatuzumab-containing pola-R-CHP backbone.

nodes.name: R-CHOP
nodes.title: Advanced, IPI 0-1: R-CHOP x 6
nodes.description: Six cycles of R-CHOP is the standard backbone for low-risk advanced DLBCL; then response is confirmed.
bullets: R-CHOP x 6 cycles (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone)
Interim and end-of-treatment PET to confirm response
Growth-factor support and tumor-lysis prophylaxis for high burden
R-CHOP regimen referenced below; then go to response assessment

nodes.name: pola-R-CHP
nodes.title: Advanced, IPI 2-5: pola-R-CHP
nodes.description: For intermediate-to-high-risk disease, polatuzumab vedotin replaces vincristine (pola-R-CHP), which improved progression-free survival versus R-CHOP; then response is confirmed.
bullets: Pola-R-CHP x 6 cycles: polatuzumab vedotin + rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, prednisone (vincristine omitted), then 2 further rituximab doses
Monitor for peripheral neuropathy and cytopenias
R-CHOP remains an acceptable alternative
Pola-R-CHP dose protocol referenced below; then go to response assessment

nodes.name: First-line response
nodes.title: End-of-first-line response assessment
nodes.description: Restage with FDG-PET at the end of first-line therapy. A complete metabolic response moves to surveillance; residual or progressive disease (biopsy-confirmed) enters the relapsed / refractory pathway.

nodes.name: Relapse workup
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory: confirm and restage
nodes.description: Confirm relapse histologically and restage before choosing a second-line strategy.
bullets: Biopsy to confirm relapse and exclude a different histology or transformation
PET/CT restaging; re-check LDH, organ function, hepatitis/HIV status
Assess fitness, prior anthracycline exposure, and candidacy for cellular therapy
Re-evaluate CNS risk and neurologic symptoms

nodes.name: Cellular-therapy fit
nodes.title: Relapsed: fit for intensive / cellular therapy?
nodes.description: Candidacy for CAR T-cell therapy or high-dose therapy with autologous transplant separates the intensive pathway from the non-intensive pathway.

nodes.name: Relapse timing
nodes.title: Fit relapse: timing / prior cellular therapy
nodes.description: Timing of relapse relative to first-line therapy, and whether the patient has already had cellular therapy or transplant, selects the second-line strategy.

options.label: Progression after prior CAR-T or transplant

nodes.name: Bridging therapy
nodes.title: Second-line CAR-T: bridging therapy?
nodes.description: While CAR T-cells are manufactured, rapidly progressive or bulky disease may need bridging therapy to maintain disease control before infusion.

nodes.name: CD19 CAR T-cell
nodes.title: Second-line CD19 CAR T-cell therapy
nodes.description: For primary-refractory disease or early relapse (and chemorefractory late relapse), CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the preferred cellular therapy; then response is confirmed.
bullets: Axicabtagene ciloleucel or lisocabtagene maraleucel (CD19 CAR-T) after lymphodepletion
Bridging therapy as decided above; manage at a certified center
Monitor for cytokine-release syndrome and neurotoxicity (ICANS)
The CAR T-cell product has no per-drug dose; the fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion dose protocol is referenced below; then go to post-CAR-T response assessment

nodes.name: Post-CAR-T response
nodes.title: Response after CAR T-cell therapy
nodes.description: Restage after CAR-T. A durable complete response moves to surveillance; relapse after CAR-T enters the post-cellular options.

nodes.name: Platinum salvage
nodes.title: Late relapse: platinum-based salvage chemoimmunotherapy
nodes.description: For relapse at or beyond 12 months in a transplant-fit patient, platinum-based salvage tests chemosensitivity before high-dose therapy; then salvage response is assessed.
bullets: Platinum-based salvage chemoimmunotherapy (e.g. R-ICE, R-DHAP, or R-GDP)
Collect stem cells if chemosensitive and transplant is planned
Restage after 2-3 cycles to judge chemosensitivity
Salvage dose protocols referenced below (R-ICE, R-DHAP, R-GDP); then go to salvage-response assessment

nodes.name: Salvage response
nodes.title: Salvage response: chemosensitive vs refractory
nodes.description: Chemosensitive disease proceeds to high-dose therapy and autologous transplant; chemorefractory disease is diverted to CD19 CAR T-cell therapy.

nodes.name: High-dose + ASCT
nodes.title: Chemosensitive: high-dose therapy + autologous transplant
nodes.description: Chemosensitive late relapse is consolidated with high-dose conditioning and autologous stem-cell transplant; then response is confirmed.
bullets: High-dose conditioning (e.g. BEAM) followed by autologous stem-cell transplant
Consider CAR-T instead if only a partial response to salvage
Supportive care through cytopenic period; infection prophylaxis
BEAM conditioning dose protocol referenced below; then go to post-transplant response assessment

nodes.name: Post-ASCT response
nodes.title: Response after autologous transplant
nodes.description: Restage after transplant. A durable complete response moves to surveillance; relapse enters the post-cellular options.

nodes.name: Non-intensive line
nodes.title: Not transplant / CAR-T eligible: line of therapy
nodes.description: For patients who are not cellular-therapy candidates, the number of prior lines guides selection among antibody-drug conjugates, immunomodulatory combinations, and bispecific antibodies.

nodes.name: Pola-BR / Tafa-len
nodes.title: Second line, non-transplant: pola-BR or tafasitamab-lenalidomide
nodes.description: Transplant-ineligible second-line options combine targeted agents with chemotherapy or immunomodulation; then response is assessed.
bullets: Polatuzumab vedotin + bendamustine + rituximab (pola-BR)
Or tafasitamab + lenalidomide for transplant-ineligible patients
Or rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) for less-fit patients
Dose protocols referenced below (pola-BR, tafasitamab-lenalidomide, R-GemOx); then go to response assessment

nodes.name: Non-intensive 2L response
nodes.title: Response after non-transplant second line
nodes.description: A response allows continued therapy and surveillance; progression advances to a CD20xCD3 bispecific antibody.

nodes.name: Bispecific antibody
nodes.title: Third line or beyond: CD20xCD3 bispecific
nodes.description: In the third-line-and-beyond setting, off-the-shelf CD20xCD3 bispecific antibodies provide durable responses; then response is assessed.
bullets: Glofitamab (fixed-duration) or epcoritamab (continuous) CD20xCD3 bispecific antibody
Step-up dosing with CRS monitoring and tumor-lysis precautions
Loncastuximab tesirine is an alternative single agent
Dose protocols referenced below (glofitamab, epcoritamab, loncastuximab tesirine); then go to response assessment

nodes.name: Bispecific response
nodes.title: Response after bispecific antibody
nodes.description: A response allows continued therapy and surveillance; progression enters the final post-cellular / palliative options.

nodes.name: Post-cellular options
nodes.title: Progression after cellular therapy: next options
nodes.description: After prior CAR-T, transplant, or bispecific, options are non-cross-resistant agents, allogeneic transplant in selected fit patients, best supportive care, or a clinical trial.
bullets: CD20xCD3 bispecific antibody (glofitamab or epcoritamab) if not already used
Loncastuximab tesirine, tafasitamab-lenalidomide, or pola-BR depending on prior exposure
Consider allogeneic transplant in selected younger, fit, chemosensitive patients
Prioritize clinical-trial enrollment and integrate palliative care
Applicable systemic dose protocols referenced below (bispecifics, loncastuximab, tafasitamab-lenalidomide, pola-BR); allogeneic transplant and trials are individualized guidance

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: Follow-up after a complete response. Most relapses occur within the first 2 years; routine surveillance imaging is limited.
bullets: History, exam, and labs (CBC, LDH) every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months to 5 years
Routine surveillance CT/PET is not recommended in asymptomatic remission; image for symptoms or exam findings
Educate on relapse symptoms; biopsy any suspected relapse before treating
Monitor for late effects: cardiac (anthracycline), second malignancy, and infection risk
